comments.author: @jackskalski3699
comments.text:
What I need is to lift the transformer paradigm. I need the model to comprehend my entire code base. I need it to be able to infer intent and not for a few files, that I hand pick but for 300k-2mln code lines. I need it not to be limited by the so-called context window, so how long our chat can get before it's too long for the model to re-consume. And most of all I need them to not forget previous features so better longevity and continuity of thought I guess. 

Perhaps the constant jumps between the highly dimensional concept space of the model and the pitty text reality needs to be lifted. So that the model is allowed to think in its own space and rules not in text. Perhaps we don't need to understand all the time how the model works so let it develops its own encoding languages and more efficient in model encodings, even if we don't understand them?

Working with these models on real c++ coding challenges with real engineering problems is still a chore. Silly small standalone web apps are not the reality. Try dropping such a model into a real rendering engine and see how well it performs... So far claud is the best.

comments.author: @BrianElliott-yx1gf
comments.text: It's not a new skill, it's an emerging trait. One that seems to be growing. I say emerging to the fact that when you do something, anything you have done a 100x before, it's happens now where you think less and get the same outcome. But, have you taken this same take and at every step when are the different ways I can do the same task, and try some to find out you have been doing this task the hard way for unknow years. Well now take grok, and seed 30 agents to do this 1st step of a task and they all report to each other, pick 1 or more paths to start the next step, then 60 or 100 agents do the next step and report back. Then later on be able to reflect back on the progress when starting the task over and do similar things with better trained agents to get better results. Emerging traits that will end up in the next grok. This can be great on the upside and terribly wrong if the AI happens to get sideways. You learn to trust it and that's where the mistake starts
